title: He didn’t fall in one day.
paragraphs:
He didn’t fall in one day.
He drifted… one compromise at a time.
And by the time the pulpit noticed—his soul was already starving.

Listen, shepherd. This is not to shame you.
This is to guard you.
Here are 7 things a pastor must avoid—or risk preaching fire with a cold heart:

1. Preaching without prayer
You can craft sermons… but only God breathes life.
Acts 6:4 — “We will give ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”
No prayer = no power.

2. Loving the spotlight more than the Savior
The stage can become an idol dressed like ministry.
But this was never about your name.
It’s about His.
John 3:30 — “He must increase, but I must decrease.”

3. Secret sin
What you hide will shape you.
What you refuse to kill will slowly kill you.
Some scholars interpret Psalm 32 as David describing the physical weight of hidden sin—bones wasting away.
You can’t lead people into freedom while you’re chained in private.

4. Neglecting your family
You win the church… but lose your home?
That’s not victory.
1 Timothy 3:5 — If a man cannot lead his own household, how can he care for God’s church?

Your first ministry has names.
They call you husband. Father.

5. People-pleasing over truth-preaching
If everyone likes you… you might not be saying what needs to be said.
Galatians 1:10 — “Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God?”

Truth wounds before it heals.
Don’t trade conviction for applause.

6. Burnout without boundaries
You are not the Messiah.
Jesus Himself withdrew (Luke 5:16).
Rest is not weakness—it’s obedience.
A tired shepherd makes careless decisions.

7. Forgetting the Gospel yourself
This is the most dangerous one.

You preach grace… but live like it’s all on you.
You call sinners to repentance… but forget you are one rescued daily.
But here’s what we miss…

Ministry doesn’t run on gifting.
It survives on grace.
And that’s where hope walks in.

Jesus didn’t just call you—He sustains you.
The same blood you preach… is the blood that covers you.
The same cross you point to… is where you must return.
Every. Single. Day.
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.

Kneel again.
Repent again.
Receive grace again.

And rise—not as a perfect pastor…
But as a dependent one.
Or better—pray for one right now.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
